message.content:
Below is a quick guide (and sample code) showing how you can pull the **first 25 resolution records** for the IP `67.89.0.1` from VirusTotal’s v3 API using your key (`sec_key5`).  
(If you run into rate‑limits or other issues, double‑check that the key has “IP Address” permissions.)

---

### 1️⃣ Endpoint & Parameters  

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip}/resolutions
```

* `{ip}` → `67.89.0.1`  
* Query param `limit=25` – returns up to 25 items per page.  
* Optional pagination token (`after`) if you need more than one page later.

> Example URL:
>
> ```
> https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1/resolutions?limit=25
> ```

---

### 2️⃣ Authentication Header  

```http
X-Apikey: sec_key5
```

VirusTotal expects the API key in the *header*, not as a query parameter.

---

### 3️⃣ Sample cURL Command  

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: sec_key5" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1/resolutions?limit=25"
```

This will return a JSON payload similar to:

```json
{
    "data": [
        {
            "_id": "...",
            "attributes": {
                "last_resolved_at": "2024-04-01T12:34:56Z",
                "resolved_ip_address": "192.168.1.10",
                ...
            }
        },
        …
    ],
    "links": { ... },
    "meta": { ... }
}
```

---

### 4️⃣ Quick Python Snippet (requests)

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "sec_key5"
BASE_URL  = "https://www.virustool.com/api/v3"

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

params = {"limit": 25}

url = f"{BASE_URL}/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1/resolutions"

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
if resp.status_code == 200:
    data = resp.json()
    # Print each resolved hostname/IP pair
    for item in data["data"]:
        attrs = item["attributes"]
        print(f'{attrs["resolved_hostname"]}: {attrs["resolved_ip_address"]}')
else:
    print("Error:", resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

Replace `"print(...)"` with whatever processing logic you prefer.

---

### 5️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind

| Item | Why It Matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Rate limits** | Free keys usually allow ~4–15 queries/minute. If you hit a limit, wait a few seconds before retrying. |
| **Pagination** | If there are >25 entries, look at the `next` link under `links`. Use its value as the `after` parameter to fetch subsequent pages. |
| **Data fields** | Each record contains `resolved_hostname`, `resolved_ip_address`, timestamps, and sometimes additional metadata like ASN info. |

---

#### TL;DR

Use a simple authenticated GET request against `/api/v3/ip_addresses/<ip>/resolutions?limit=25`.  
Either paste the cURL line above into your terminal or copy the Python snippet into a small script—both will give you the first 25 resolution records for `67.89.0.1`.

Happy hunting!
